summary.text: Grace Meng is the incumbent U.S. Representative for New York's 6th Congressional District, first elected in 2012. A Queens native and former public-interest lawyer, she served in the New York State Assembly before Congress and is the first Asian American member of Congress from New York. She is the Ranking Member of the Appropriations Subcommittee on Commerce, Justice, Science, and Related Agencies and chairs the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus.

paragraphs.text: Meng was born in Queens, New York, in 1975; her official biography says she was born in Elmhurst and raised in Elmhurst, Bayside, and Flushing, and that she graduated from Stuyvesant High School.
She attended the University of Michigan and earned a law degree from Yeshiva University's Benjamin N. Cardozo School of Law.
She worked as a public-interest lawyer before entering public service.
Meng won the Democratic primary for New York State Assembly District 22 in 2008 and the general election that November; she was re-elected in 2010 and served until entering Congress in 2013.

In 2012 she won the Democratic primary for New York's 6th District over Assembly member Rory Lancman, City Council member Elizabeth Crowley, and Robert Mittman, then won the general election and took office in January 2013.

She serves on the House Appropriations Committee; her official biography lists her as Ranking Member of the Commerce, Justice, Science, and Related Agencies Subcommittee and a member of the National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Subcommittee.
Meng's official biography describes her as the first and only Asian American member of Congress from New York State and the first female member of Congress from Queens since Geraldine Ferraro.

She chairs the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus and co-chairs the House Bipartisan Taskforce for Combatting Antisemitism, and her official biography lists enacted bills including the COVID-19 Hate Crimes Act and a law striking "Oriental" from federal law.
She lives in Queens with her husband and their two sons, according to her official biography.
